title: Completed coefficient units: finite Tor bounds and coherent pullback
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, as in [def-pur-conventions]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_W$, $U_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}[0]$ for $W=X,Y$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Use completed derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], coherent reductions [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and normalized quotient systems [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower].

The object $U_W$ belongs to $D^b_{ctf}(W,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], with every reduction canonically $B_{W,n}[0]$, cohomological interval $[0,0]$ and Tor interval $[0,0]$, uniformly in $n$. Its quotient system has the single constructible stratum $W$.

The finite coefficient-unit multiplications $Lf_n^*B_{Y,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}B_{X,n}$ constitute an isomorphism of whole normalized derived systems, commuting with the actual quotient transitions. Under the specified derived-limit construction of completed pullback they induce an isomorphism
$$u_f:Lf^*U_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}U_X.$$
Its coherent reduction is precisely that system map, not merely an unspecified family of isomorphisms of objects. The images of $u_f$ under rationalization [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the common-stage inclusion [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] are the unit identifications $Lf_E^*E_Y\cong E_X$ and $Lf_\Omega^*\Omega_Y\cong\Omega_X$ for the pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. In particular $U_Y$ is an integral lattice presenting these two coefficient units. The integral unit here is the completed coefficient sheaf, not the discrete constant $\mathcal O_E$-sheaf.

proof.text: Apply completedUnitAdmissible over the literal field and its canonical small model. Constructibility and the actual reduction isomorphisms come from the constant coefficient theorem. The regular single complex is a finite flat model, which gives uniform cohomological and Tor interval [0,0].

Use completedUnitReduction for X and Y. Its finite identifications preserve sections, its comparison has the actual finite reduction maps, and its augmentation is the actual adjunction unit followed by limit of the strict comparison. Transfer reduction_normalized across the comparison isomorphisms.

Mathlib pullbackObjUnitToUnit is invertible for a final base functor. Pro-etale base change and its product with identity on the coefficient levels are final, so both finite and whole-system multiplications are isomorphisms. Exact functor localization and the specified single comparison make systemMap an isomorphism. Its finite components are computed by the normalized finite adjunction mate.

Choose the normalized completed primitive counit realization. Compose its component with total limit of pullback of the Y comparison and systemMap, and then inverse of the X augmentation. This is the required unit isomorphism with its definitional unit_formula. The augmentation equality and the adjunction triangle identify reduction of its inverse leg with the counit. Counit naturality gives coherent_reduction as an equality of whole-system arrows.

Lift the integral unit isomorphism to the full constructible integral category, apply raw rationalization, and prepend the specified rational-source equality transport. These are all isomorphisms. The small-model scalar naturality lemma gives model_square. The common-stage map is its specified source transport followed by the inclusion functor applied to the literal-field rational map, hence it too is an isomorphism.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q37-e63085868 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Q37 lem-pur-completed-unit-pullback-tower e6308586. The delivery adds no new nodes and leaves the statement and stmt_deps unchanged. It is a first split: there is no repair note, and the item is still unsplit in live and side-live. I read all 6 steps and the statement of every cited node. Step 1: lem-weil-constant-scalar-strict-unit with L=E gives the K-flat unit, the u_m multiplication isomorphisms commuting with every transition, and u_m∘γ_m=π_m. Step 2: lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit (Bhatt–Scholze Prop 3.1.10) plus transport along ∏u_n gives the Roos triangle with first map c, hence derived completeness. Step 3: the single stratum W, with cohomological and Tor bounds [0,0] uniformly in n; ℓ is invertible on these k-schemes; W=∅, n=1 and ramified E all check out. Step 4: prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map and prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact hold for arbitrary f, and the quotient square holds on constant sections. Step 5: counit naturality and the triangle identity give b_X R(u_f)=d·e, which I checked by hand. Step 6: the rational and common-stage arrow formulas follow from the definitions. FIX (C1/E5): Step 5 asserted a_X = L_X(b_X)∘u without justification, and that identity carries the coherent-reduction clause. I added the argument: by lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus the unit's level-n composite is the reduction map, and by lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison a_X has level composites π_n, so clause 3 of lem-weil-proetale-surjective-tower-derived-limit (with G=R_X) forces equality. I also cited the cone/total-limit comparison behind Lf^*U_Y=L_X(F_f𝓑_Y). In Step 4 I defined the previously undefined F_f and cited def-pur-integral-derived-operations. I recomputed proof_deps and added a tool_uses entry for the evaluation-calculus node. None of the added citations creates a cycle. Advisory: Steps 2–3 re-prove existing statements, namely lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible (2) and the derived-completeness clause of lem-weil-constant-scalar-unit-quasi-isomorphism; these could simply be cited. theorem completedUnitPullbackTower (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [IsSeparated (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [IsSeparated (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [f.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] :
    Nonempty (Result P f)
